summary: Slow initial chat response and intermittent completion timeouts after runtime 1.6 + quantized model rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Nimbus Health began seeing increased latency for the first chat response and occasional completion timeouts after we rolled runtime 1.6 and a new quantized model variant (rwd-v2-small-quant) to production in us-east-1. Impact: intermittent UX degradation for chat product (initial spinner > 5s, sporadic 504s at the client).

Impact:
- ~20% of user chat sessions experience initial response > 3s, 5% > 8s during peak window (13:00-14:00 UTC).
- Several customer requests resulted in HTTP 504 from edge after 60s (timeout path) — reported by customer and corroborated in our API gateway logs.

Environment:
- Runtime: 1.6.0 (rolled 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC)
- Model: rwd-v2-small-quant pinned by rollout policy for tiered routing
- Region: prod-us-east (primary cluster)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer issues chat completions against /v1/chat with model=rwd-v2-small-quant. 2) Start a fresh chat session with a 3-10 sentence prompt with 1k token budget. 3) Observe initial response latency and occasional timeout after ~60s. 4) Repeating the same request within a warmed session reduces latency. 5) Incidence higher for new sessions and when traffic shifts to a new router lane after model routing changes.
logs:
- API Gateway traces: repeated upstream 504s at 13:18:42Z for connection pool entry timeout.
- Serving runtime logs: container start time for affected pods shows up to 900ms cold-start time plus 200-400ms additional stall at first generate call.
- Scheduler metrics: queue_depth spikes at 95th percentile coincident with rollout batch windows.
- KV-cache metrics: miss_rate increased from 3% baseline to 41% in the affected window for rwd-v2-small-quant prefix keys.
- Kernel selection: audit logs show fallback to reference_attention for ~12% of initial requests due to mis-detected attention pattern in compiled kernel selector.
- No elevated GPU utilization or OOMs observed.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypotheses:
- (A) Prefix/KV cache invalidation on model swap causing first-request work to rebuild cache and stall first token. Evidence: high KV cache miss rate and faster latencies for warmed sessions.
- (B) Kernel selector fallback path triggered for certain batching shapes leading to slower reference implementation for first chunk. Evidence: kernel audit entries show reference_attention fallback for initial requests.
- (C) Routing/scheduler burst behavior or container prewarm policy not firing resulting in brief queueing at canary/beta lanes. Evidence: queue_depth spikes around rollout times and increased cold starts logged.

What we ran so far:
- Correlated API gateway traces with pod logs and discovered the 504s align with higher miss_rate for KV cache and a small population of containers reporting the reference kernel fallback.
- Reproduced locally by running rwd-v2-small-quant with an empty KV cache; observed ~600-1200ms extra latency on initial generate compared to warmed run.
- Temporary traffic steering: manually moved ~30% of Nimbus traffic to runtime 1.5 in us-east for mitigation; observed immediate drop in >3s initial responses for that cohort.
- Enabled additional prewarm for new pods in us-east cluster; saw reduced cold-start incidence but residual kernel fallback stalls remain.

Next steps:
- Engineering to patch kernel selector to avoid spurious fallback for quantized variant (PR linked).
- Add targeted prewarming of KV cache keys for pinned models during rollout windows.
- Tighten autoscaling and scheduler prewarm policy for canary lanes during rollouts.
- Notify Nimbus with recommended temporary pin to runtime=1.5 or add header X-RW-Warm: true to force warmed path in their integration as a workaround.

resolution_notes:
Workaround implemented: steering customer traffic to runtime 1.5 reduced incidents. Recommended customer pin to runtime=1.5 or add X-RW-Warm header for immediate relief.
Permanent fix: runtime kernel selector patch merged (PR #2431) to correct quantized attention detection; scheduled canary rollout 2026-03-15 with KV cache warmup job during rollout windows.
Follow-up: create runbook for model rollout warmup (task INT-430) and add automated prewarm in the deployment pipeline. Customer notified and SRE to monitor next 48h post patch.
notes_for_follow_up:
- Verify KV cache miss_rate returns to baseline after warmup job.
- Confirm 95th percentile initial response latency decrease for pinned customers.
- Update runbook and include a checklist for rolling quantized models.
- Postmortem to be created if patch does not fully resolve within 72 hours.
